In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of optimization-based DSS can significantly reduce costs for meeting TMDLs.
the cost-effectiveness of stormwater management is highly dependent on the placement of the stormwater management practices and that optimization can be used to find the optimal placement.
the use of a decision support system for TMDL management is cost-effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a DSS can help urban watershed managers to develop least-cost strategies for TMDL implementation.
the DSS can be a valuable tool for cities to meet TMDL requirements in the least costly manner.
a DSS for urban runoff control can be developed by coupling a hydrologic model with a mixed integer linear program for selecting least-cost filter placement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cost-effective TMDL compliance can be achieved through a phased, least cost approach using stormwater filters, and that a DSS is a powerful tool for urban watershed management to achieve compliance.
the cost-effectiveness of stormwater management can be greatly increased by using a decision support system to identify optimal locations and configurations for stormwater treatment devices.
cost-effective solutions to urban runoff management can be found by using optimization models that consider the spatial and temporal characteristics of urban drainage networks.
